name: Konomihu
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

earlier_scan.source_named: Silver, Shirley. 1980. Shasta and Konomihu (IJAL/Shastan materials); Dixon 1905; Golla 2011:90-95 — extinct, poorly attested; no copy reachable online

sources.citation: Kroeber, A. L. 1925. Handbook of the Indians of California. BAE Bulletin 78. Section 'The Konomihu', pp. 283-284
sources.note: Nothing. Classification and ethnography only: 'The Konomihu are the most divergent of the marginal Shastan tribes... questionable whether their speech is more properly a highly specialized aberration of Shasta or of an ancient and independent but moribund branch of Hokan' (p. 283).

sources.citation: Dixon, Roland B. 1907. The Shasta. Bulletin of the American Museum of Natural History 17(5): 381-498 (Appendix: The Konomi'hu, pp. 495-498)
sources.note: Nothing. Ethnographic note plus the only published Konomihu vocabulary (~55 items, pp. 497-498, e.g. ki'poman 'hand', kum'ma 'water', tamma'hawe 'eat'); forms carry a raised accent mark but the paper gives no orthographic key and no statement about stress (grep for accent/stress/phonet finds nothing in the whole bulletin).

sources.citation: Dixon, Roland B. 1905. The Shasta-Achomawi: A New Linguistic Stock, with Four New Dialects. American Anthropologist n.s. 7(2): 213-217. DOI 10.1525/aa.1905.7.2.02a00030
sources.note: Nothing. Reports that two Shasta women recalled 'some seventy-five words and short phrases' of Konomihu (p. 214); says 'the general phonetic character of the language is entirely in accord with the Shasta' (p. 214); gives a 17-item comparative table (p. 216) whose forms carry acute accent marks (e.g. kin'nux, axta', gamga'tsineau) but no rule or remark on stress placement.

sources.citation: California Language Archive, Konomihu language page (cla.berkeley.edu/languages/) and archive item listing (langid=255)
sources.note: Nothing; lists Golla 2011, Larsson 1987 and Silver 1980 as the references; the item listing is JavaScript-rendered and came back empty.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid page kono1241 and Wikipedia 'Konomihu language' / 'Shastan languages'
sources.note: Nothing on phonology; Glottolog lists no descriptive reference of its own, citing only Golla 2011:90-95, Silver 1980, Dixon 1905, Larsson 1987 ('an extinct poorly attested somewhat mysterious Shastan language'); Wikipedia notes an unpublished 1928 de Angulo wordlist and Silver 1980's comparison with Shasta.
